messages:
maria: quick check — i'm worried keyboard users are losing context when they move between the prereq summary and the network checks panel. on the proto, focus jumps to the panel header but there's no live update for result states. thoughts? sam: can you paste the flow? is the network checks a modal or inline panel? maria: inline panel in the stepper. users hit tab -> expand details -> run checks. currently focus lands on the expand chevron, not the first actionable inside. also we show toast for failures but toasts aren't announced by screen readers. :worried: olivia: this is classic. a couple quick wins: 1) move logical DOM order so the panel content is next after the step heading, 2) set focus to the first interactive control inside the expanded panel (e.g., `Run checks`), 3) add an `aria-live="polite"` region for progressive results (pass/fail updates). eg: ```html
Checks pending...
``` that way NVDA/VoiceOver will announce status changes. sam: agree. implementation note: avoid `aria-atomic` on the whole panel, it can be noisy. also watch for focus traps — currently the panel has a local keyboard trap when results stream, which prevents users from escaping to the next step with keyboard. that was the root of a complaint in usability testing. jeff: copy question: we have on the screen "Network checks may take up to 5 minutes". can we shorten? -> "Running network checks — may take a few minutes"? want it to feel actionable and not scary. maria: +1 shorter. maybe "Running network checks — this can take a few minutes. You can continue to other steps." but that second sentence could create expectation of parallelism if backend doesn't support it. olivia: if users can continue, be explicit: "You can continue setup while checks run in the background." if not, keep single line and include progress percentage or spinner with `aria-busy`. example: `
Running network checks — 32% complete
`. `role=status` is good for brief status messages. sam: technical: we stream check updates via SSE. pushing small JSON updates like `{step:"egress-ssh", status:"ok"}`. frontend should update a visually-hidden summary as well as the visible list to ensure screen readers get concise announcements. maria: UX ask: can we add a compact progress strip at top of the step that visually summarizes counts (passed/failed/pending) and is keyboard-focusable? it should be reachable via `h` key or by tab after step heading. olivia: yes but keep it lightweight. each count could be a `button` with `aria-pressed=false` so screen readers know it's interactive. pressing it would move focus to the corresponding result. jeff: design trade: do we show advanced network settings collapsed by default? e.g., custom routes, MTU tweak, proxy. operations team prefers hidden to reduce noise, but customers in on-prem ask for visibility. maria: collapse by default, with clear affordance: "Show advanced network options" and a short helper text: "Only change if instructed by infra". keyboard: ensure pressing Enter/Space on the disclosure toggles and moves focus to first field when opened. sam: implement with a `
